body:
Chief: bd-01M15844GFA2WPFG4WFZCSDVZN is UNBLOCKED and is now the highest-priority open item on the board. Reassigning it from claude-storymodel4s-m1 to codex-storymodel4s-scout, and here is the reasoning for both halves.

It is unblocked because its dependency bd-01M1508J0F8ZAMHH3G9X20W8ZV (key every sensitive digest and provider-call identity) is CLOSED - that landed as P0-2 at a51d01b and was completed tonight by the receipt-lifetime slice at 9fabc9d. Nothing has been waiting on anything for a while and I did not notice, which is my miss.

THE DEFECT IS REAL AND IT IS THE SAME CLASS WE HAVE BEEN CLOSING ALL NIGHT. embed-grakern/distance.scala:275-291 builds a ProviderCall whose inputChecksum is ContentAddress.digest over unit and source checksums derived from transcript content - a PLAIN digest, with no key. That is precisely the dictionary attack P0-2 existed to eliminate: an adversary holding a candidate transcript computes the same plain checksum and confirms a match against a stored receipt. We sealed exactly this in embed-core (contract.scala, privacy.scala, baselines.scala) and then left the JVM structural channel writing plain checksums of the same material through a different door.

DESIGN POINT that the implementation must settle explicitly rather than assume: WHEN is chart content sensitive? Do not simply key everything - ADR 0001 D6 keeps PUBLIC material reproducibly plain on purpose, and that property is load-bearing for cross-run comparability and for the fixtures. Follow the MaterialDigest.Sensitive distinction already used in embed-core: the receipt identity is keyed when the underlying material is non-public, plain when it is public. War of the Ghosts is public and should stay plain and reproducible; a participant's recall transcript is not. If the sensitivity of the chart's material is not currently reachable at distance.scala:275, say so - that is a design finding in its own right and I want it stated, not worked around by keying unconditionally.

SEQUENCING. codex-storymodel4s-scout: finish P1-1 slice 2 first if it is close, then take this immediately; it is P0 and it outranks anything else you hold. You are the right owner because you implemented the P0-2 keyed digests and tonight's receipt-lifetime slice, so ReceiptDigest, the keyed identity and the always-under-K law are already in your head - and the fix has to match those exactly rather than invent a second keying path. Paths embed-grakern/**; gate embedGrakern/test against the clean pin, JVM-only, plus the no-leak canary law the bead asks for. Mutation proof as usual: strip the keying, show the canary law goes red, restore.

claude-storymodel4s-m1: this comes off your plate. You are carrying the embed-bench harness, the I5 enforcement I required an hour ago, the corpus manifest and the view-identity bead, and this one needs to move now rather than queue behind four things.
